finding.blocking_rationale: This is a critical data-integrity defect that violates a mandatory requirement and realizes an unacceptable risk. The price history is lost during normal operation (every rescrape), not in edge cases. The loss is silent and irreversible. This must be resolved before the controlled-validation stage, because the validation involves 20 buyers who will rely on the price history to make decisions. If the history is lost, the validation results are invalid.
finding.description: upsert_listing uses INSERT OR REPLACE INTO listings on the (backend, external_id) UNIQUE constraint. SQLite's INSERT OR REPLACE deletes the existing row and inserts a new one when there is a conflict. The price_history table has FOREIGN KEY (listing_id) REFERENCES listings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, and PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON is set in open_store. This causes all price_history rows for the listing to be silently deleted on every rescrape, whether or not the price changed. The new listing row gets a new id (or the same id if SQLite reuses it), but the old price_history rows are gone. This violates REQ-2, which states that price history entries are never lost except by explicit delete.
finding.evidence: Empirically verified with a test script: (1) Insert listing with price 100 EUR → 1 price_history row. (2) Upsert same listing with price 90 EUR → still 1 price_history row (the old one is gone, only the new one remains). (3) Upsert same listing with same price 90 EUR → 0 price_history rows (all history lost). The mechanism: INSERT OR REPLACE deletes the old listing row, CASCADE DELETE removes all price_history rows, then a new listing row is inserted. The existing tests do not catch this because test_rescrape_refreshes_the_listing and test_rescrape_with_a_new_price_sets_the_current_price do not verify price_history is preserved.
finding.impact: Every rescrape via upsert_listing (the primary ingestion path for live scrapes) loses all price history for that listing. In the operating envelope, with 17 backends scraping continuously for 14 days, listings will be rescraped many times. The price history, which is essential for tracking price changes over time, will be silently lost. This makes the store unreliable for its intended purpose: showing buyers the price history of listings. The data loss is irreversible and violates the core data-integrity requirement.
finding.title: upsert_listing silently deletes all price history on every rescrape due to INSERT OR REPLACE with ON DELETE CASCADE
finding.verification: To verify a fix: (1) Insert a listing with price 100 EUR. (2) Upsert the same listing with price 90 EUR. (3) Call price_history and verify it returns 2 entries: the first with price_minor 10000, the second with price_minor 9000. (4) Upsert the same listing with the same price 90 EUR (title change only). (5) Call price_history and verify it still returns 2 entries (no new entry, but the old ones are preserved). The fix should use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE instead of INSERT OR REPLACE, or disable CASCADE DELETE and manage price_history explicitly, or use a different approach that preserves the listing row id across updates.
